If you would like to participate in this meeting, you can participate via the following
options:

1. VIEW THE MEETING LIVE ONLINE AT: https://youtube.com/@SouthGateCA90280
Please allow up to 24 hours after the meeting for the archive to be available.
2. PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING by emailing the City Clerk at:

"Public Comment" in the subject line.
3. ATTEND THE MEETING IN PERSON
*The disruption in service of any alternative method does not prelude the City Council
or other legislative
body from taking further action and moving forward on the agenda.

Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials

on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City

  4

comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items

Agenda Items 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including
Ordinances, Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent
Calendar, individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion
of these items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific
items be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members
of the public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three
(3) minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may

  9
 adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

  PURPOSE:  To review  an agreement  between  the City,  Alameda  Engle Properties,  LLC  ("AEP"),
  Fleet Yards,  Inc. ("Fleet  Yards"),  and the City listing  the terins  and timeline  for the ternnination  of

  monitoring,  and the transition  of the property  at 8530  Alameda  Street,  South  Gate  ("Subject
  Property")  to a legally  allowable  use.

  PROJECT  OVERVIEW

  Proiect Location:  8530 Alameda  Street
  Assessor's  Parcel Number:  6202-036-003
  Property  Owner:  Alameda  Engle  Properties  (Jason Engle)
  Tenant/Occupant:  Fleet Yards,  Inc. (Daniel  Otting)
  Appellant/Representative:  Sara Atsbaha,  Somos  Law  Group
  General  Plan Designation:  Industrial  (Cornrnunity  Design  Element,  Figure  CD 1,
  Existing  Land Uses)
  South  Gate College  District  Subarea 1 (Community  Design
  Element,  Figure  CD 4, Districts)
  7.  :  IF (Industrial  Flex)

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:
  1.  DISCUSS  a proposed  agreement  for the teri'nination  of all truck  trailer  storage,  the removal  of
  all trucks  trailers,  the implementation  of air quality  monitoring,  and the transition  of the
  property  at 8530 Alameda  Street,  South  Gate ("Subject  Property")  to a legally  allowable  use;
  2.  ACCEPT  the determination  that  this  matter  is exempt  from  tlie  California  Environi'nental
  Quality  Act;
  3.  AUTHORIZE  the City Manager  to execute  agreement  included  in Attachment  1.

  ENVIRONMENT  AL  EV ALUATION
  The City  Council's  detennination  on an agreement  to tenninate  a use is not subject  to California
  Environmental  Quality  Act (CEQA)  review  because it is not an "approval"  as defined  in California
  Code of Regulations,  Title  14, Section  15352,  but rather  an agreement  to terminate  a use at a site,

  28
 and therefore  does not coinrnit  the City to any definite  course of action regarding  a new use on the
subject  property.  Furthert'nore,  CEQA  does not apply  to projects  which  a public  agency  rejects  or

disapproves  pursuant  to Section  15270(a).

BACKGROUND
Notwithstanding  the erroneous  issuance  of a Temporary  Use Permit  in July 2020,  City  Staff has
diligently  and consistently  been seeking  the termination  of the use ofthe  Subject  Property  for truck
trailer  storage  - including  by denying  any extension  of Temporaiy  Use Permit  TUP  2020-01,
rejecting  any assertion  by Alameda  Engle  Properties  ("AEP")  and/or  Fleet Yards  that such use is
not legal,  nonconforming  and must  otherwise  cease, and recoinmending  denial  of any change  of
zone for the Subject  Property  and amendments  to the zoning  of the Subject  Property  or the General
Plan that would  otherwise  allow  such use to continue.

As a result  of the City's  efforts,  AEP  has exercised  its due process  rights  to appeal  first  to the
Planning  Commission  and subsequently  to the City  Council,  the the Community  Development
Director's  decision  to deny  any extension  of TUP  2020-01  and the Community  Development
Director's  determination  that the use of the Subject  Property  for truck  trailer  storage  is not a legal,
nonconforming  use and that it must otherwise  tenninate  (hereinafter,  "Appeals").  AEP's  Appeals
and the public  hearing  regarding  AEP's  application  for a zone change and general  plan amendment
(hereinafl:er,  collectively,  "Public  Hearings")  were scheduled  for April  22, 2025.

At tlie Public  Hearings  on April  22, 2025, AEP requested  a continuance  of the Public  Hearings  to
negotiate  the terms  of an Agreement  with  the City  to terminate  all use of the Subject  Property  for
truck  trailer  storage  - wliich,  once entered,  AEP  would  withdraw  its Appeals  and its application

ANALYSIS:
City  Staff  has diligently  and consistently  been seeking  the termination  of the use of the Subject
Property  for truck  trailer  storage  - however,  the City  is required  to ensure  tliat  AEP  and Fleet
Yards  are provided  with  their  due process  rights  pursuant  to the US Constitution  and California
Constitution.  These due process  rights  include  AEP's  right  to challenge  decisions  that have been
made  by the Comi'nunity  Development  Director  to the Plai'ining  Commission  - and the right  to
appeal the Planning  Comt'nission's  decision  to the City  Council.

During  the course  of these proceedings,  City  Staff has sought  AEP's  voluntary  compliance  with
existing  laws  and the  General  Plan,  however,  City  Staff  was  unwilling  to recommend  any

agreement  with  AEP based upon AEP's  desire to be granted  ten (10) years to terininate  tlie truck
trailer  storage  use of the Subject  Property.  In consideration  of AEP's  and Fleet Yards'  refusal  to
terminate  the truck  trailer  storage  use in a timely  fashion  - and in consideration  of the health  and
safety  concerns  raised  by the public,  City  Staff  has steadfastly  moved  forward  with  the Public
Hearings  required  for the City  to lawfully  terminate  the truck  trailer  storage  use of tlie Subject
Property.

AEP  and Fleet Yards  is now prepared  to enter into an agreement  with  the City which  would  result
in,  amongst  other benefits,  the following:

  a)  Teri'nination  of all truck  trailer  and container  storage  at the Subject  Property  on or
  before  May  13, 2026;

  b)  Ternnination  of all tnick  trailer  and container  storage  at the parcel  contiguous  to the
  Subject  Property  (that is located  in unincorporated  Los Angeles  County)  on or before
  May 13, 2026;

  c)  Implementation  of specified  air quality  monitoring  efforts  to address  envirorunental
  concerns;

  d)  Immediate  withdrawal  of all Appeals  and the request  for a zone change  and General
  Plan Amendment,  as well  as a waiver  of any claims  and/or  causes of action  AEP and/or
  Fleet  Yards  may  have  against  the City  related  to the subject  matter  of the Public
  Hearings;  and,

  3
   e)  Assurances  from  AEP  that it will  seek an allowable  use of the Subject  Property,  and
  that it will  otherwise  adhere to all applicable  laws - including  the Zoning  Ordinance
  and General  Plan.

There  are a number  of reasons why the City  Council  may consider  the settlement  agreement  as the
best option  to achieve  compliance,  including:

  1.  City  Staff  and the coinmunity  share concerns  about the truck  trailer  and container  storage
  on both  the Subject  Property  in South  Gate and upon  the contiguous  property  located  in
  unincorporated  Los Angeles  County  creating  and/or  contributing  to nuisance  activities  and
  conditions,  as well  as potential  health  and safety  hazards.  Settlement  by means  of the
  proposed  Agreement  would  lead to the applicant's  voluntary  coinmitment  to terminate  all
  truck  trailer  and container  storage  activities  on the City  and County  propeities  - thereby
  eliminating  all adverse  impacts  from  these activities  upon  our coinmunity.  Without  this
  Agreement,  any decision  by the City  Council  on the Public  Hearings  would  have no impact
  upon the property  in the unincorporated  County  - and would  likely  result  in AEP  and/or
  Fleet Yards  continuing  current  operations  on the County  side.

  2.  The Agreement  would  result  in the teri'nination  of all truck  trailer  and container  storage  -
  including  the removal  of all truck  trailers  and containers  from  the Subject  Property  (and
  the contiguous  property  in LA  County)  by a date certain  - on or before  May  13, 2026.  A
  one-year  transition  period  will  allow  the applicant  to transition  to an acceptable  use.

  3.  The Agreement  provides  for specified  air quality  monitoring  by AEP,  and would  require
  AEP to work  proactively  with the City to ensure that environmental  conceriis  are addressed
  under the Agreement.

  4.  Entering  into the Agreement  would  result in the voluntary  withdrawal  of all Appeals  - and
  would  result  in the previous  decisions  by the Planning  Coinrnission  (to deny the extension
  of the TUP,  that the metal  processing/recycling  activities  have been abandoned,  and that
  the truck  trailer  and container  storage  is not legal,  nonconforming)  to be final  and binding
  and not subject  to further  challenge  by AEP  or Fleet Yards.

  5.  Should  the  City  Council  reject  the Agreement,  and,  instead,  proceed  with  the  Public
  Hearings,  any decision  adverse  to AEP's  and/or  Fleet  Yards'  interests  would  likely  be
  appealed  and/or  challenged  in the Superior  Court  - and, if necessary,  appealed  to higher
  couits  thereafter.  If litigated,  the applicant  may employ  tactics  to delay immediate  closure,
  including  seeking  a temporary  restraining  order and/or  preliminary  injunction  staying  any
  decisions  of the City  Council.  Such appeals could result in a delay in terminating  the truck
  trailer  and container  storage  for rip to 2 to 3 years.

  6.  The outcome  of litigation  is uncertain.  Litigation  is also costly  and time-consuming,  and
  could  require  dedicated  City  resources  for two to three years.  Regardless  of the outcome,
  the City  could  expect  to pay in excess of $350,000  to defend  against  litigation.

  7.  The applicant  will  also likely  seek damages  from  the loss of its tenant,  rental  income  and
  business  interniption,  estimated  to be upwards  of  $11,000,000  based  on current  rent
  multiplied  by tlie expected  timeframe  to complete  litigation.  AEP  will  also likely  seek a
  finding  of  inverse  condemnation  obligating  the  City  to pay just  compensation  for  a

  31
   regulatory  taking  of the property,  which  is valued  at approximately  $60,000,000.

  8.  AEP  has a financial  interest  in seeing the property  re-purposed  for an appropriate  use for
  long-term  investment.  Although  transition  to an allowable,  pernnitted  use may take up to
  1 year,  it would  likely  be sooner.  The applicant  would  iinmediately  begin  the process  to
  repurpose  the property  to avoid  gaps in rental  income,

  9.  Once  litigation  is commenced,  neither  AEP  nor Fleet  Yards  are likely  to enter  into  an
  agreement  with  terms favorable  to tlie City - and might  reject  any and all future  settlement
  discussions  and/or  offers.  If AEP  does entertain  settlement  discussions  with  tlie City  a'Jier
  the commencement  of litigation,  the applicant  may request  payment  for the loss of rental
  income  and business  interniption,  as well  as other perceived  damages.

  10. Under  a settlement  agreement,  the applicant  would  agree to indemnify  and defend  the City
  against  any  CEQA  challenge.  The  City  has authority  to issue  an abatement  schedule
  pursuant  to its enforcement  powers.  . The  one-year  transition  period  in the settlement
  agreement  is well  within  this allotted  timeframe.

  The City  Council  has the options  to (i) enter into tlie Agreement  - and all appeals and applications
  by AEP  will  be witlidrawn;  or (ii) reject  the Agreement  and proceed  with  the Public  Hearings.

BACKGROUND
This  is an appeal  filed  by legal  counsel,  Somos  Law  Group  ("Somos"),  on behalf  of the property
owner  and applicant,  Alameda  Engle  Properties,  LLC  ("AEP"  represented  by Jason  Engle),  for  a
6.78-acre  property  located  at  8530  Alameda  Street.  Somos  is  appealing  the  Planning
Commission's  decision  on the Director  of Community  Development's  determination.

It should  be noted  that AEP  also owns  the abutting  2.9-acre  site to the north  at 8440  S. Alameda
Street,  which  is located  outside  of the  City  and  in the County  of Los  Angeles.  Access  to both
properties  is via a driveway  from  Alameda  Street  to the property  at 8440  S. Alameda  Street.  This
property  is also being  used  for  truck  trailer  storage  and according  to County  staff,  a conditional
use permit  ("CUP")  is currently  being  processed.

History  of Zoning and Land Use of Subiect Property
As  early  as 1961,  the Subject  Property  was  designated  as being  within  a Heavy  Manufacturing
("M-3")  Zone.

Based  upon  a review  of public  records  and documents  submitted  by AEP,  the Site  was  used  by
Jack Engel  & Company  (hereinafter,  "JECO")  and/or  AEP  for ametal  processing/recycling  facility
from  as early  as 1973  until  approximately  March  2020.  During  that time,  the site was developed
with  a single-story  industrial  structure  used for the recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO  and/or
AEP.

The metal  recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO  and/or  AEP  included,  but was not limited  to,
the delivery  of scrap metal  product  to the Site inside  of truck  trailers  - which  would  remain  on site
for up to several  months  while  the scrap  metal  was  sorted  and processed  on-site  and prepared  for
shipment  to a final  off-site  destination.

In 1988,  the  City  amended  its  Zoning  Code,  in part,  to require  a Conditional  Use  Permit  for
recycling  facilities.  Thereafter,  on or about  April  28, 2015,  the City  Council  adopted  Ordinance

 2323, which  further  amended  the Zoning  Code and changed  the zoning  classification  of the Subject
Property  to Industrial  Flex ("IF")  Zone.

Pursuant  to the Section  11.21.030  and Table  11.21-3  of the amended  Zoning  Code,  recycling
facilities  require  a Conditional  Use Permit  - however,  tlie recycling  operations  at the Subject
Property  were  deemed  to be a legal,  nonconfon'ning  land  use that was allowed  to continue  in

According  to public  records  and infoimation  submitted  by AEP and/or its representatives,  all metal

Site.

AEP has confirnned  that around  March  2020, Fleet Yards,  Inc. comi'nenced  utilizing  the Site solely
for the storage  of truck  trailers  and/or  containers  as a principal  use.  Moreover,  the structure  that
was previously  utilized  to conduct  the metal recycling  at the Site was demolished.

On July 16, 2020,  the City  approved  Fleet Yards,  Inc.'s  application  for a Temporary  Use Pen'nit
and issued TUP2020-01,  authorizing  the use of the Subject  Property  for "truck  trailer  storage  for
a one-year  period  with  possible  one-year  extensions  up to a maximum  period  of five  years from
the  date  of  approval".  The  Community  Development  Director  explicitly  imposed  various

  2.  The approval  of the temporary  use was set to expire  on July  16, 2021  - and a new

  approval  for up to a maximum  period  of 5 years from  the original  approval  date of July
  16, 2020  - and would  be deteri'nined  based upon  compliance  with  the conditions  of
  approval  and written  verification  from  the property  owner  that the owner  is in process
  of developing  the land, selling  the land, and/or  working  with  Los Angeles  Cornrnunity
  College  or a developer  on a housing  development  project.

TUP2020-01  expired  on July 16, 2021, without  a timely  request  for renewal  from  Fleet Yards,  Inc.

Temporary  Use Permit  (or the renewal  of TUP2020-01).  In December  2022, the Director  advised

ANALYSIS:

The renewal  application  was denied  because  under  the SGMC:  (1) the use which  is the subject  of
the Temporary  Use Permit  is prohibited  at 8530 Alameda;  and (2) Temporary  Use Permits  can
only allow  otherwise  unauthorized  uses to be conducted  for a few days, not for multi-year  periods.

Past/Proposed  Use of Property  is as a "Truck  Storage/Terminal":  Applicant  and its tenant  have
been using  the subject  property  to store trucks,  truck-trailers,  and storage  containers.  Under  the
SGMC,  this use is defined  as "truck  storage/terminal"  use which,  pursuant  to the SGMC  Section
11.60.230  "T"  definitions,  "means  indoor  or outdoor  site for fireight,  truck  terminals,  truck  storage
yards,  or similar  commercial  facilities."
SGMC  Prohibits  that Use at 8530 Alameda  Street:  The subject  property  is zoned  Industrial  Flex
(IF). Table  11.21-3,  under  SGMC  Section  11.21.030  "Land  use permissions  tables",  lists allowed
land uses within  the IF zone. Truck  storage/terminal  use is not listed  on that Table  as an allowed
use within  the IF zone.  SGMC  Section  11.21.020  notes that "Any  land use that is not specifically
listed  in the land use tables  for the applicable  zone shall not be allowed  or permitted  within  the
zone."  Therefore,  the storage  of trucks,  truck-trailers  and containers  is a prohibited  use in the IF

   zone.

  Temporary  Use Pen'nits  Cannot  Autliorize  Prol'iibited  Uses for Extended  Durations.  Pursuant  to
  SGMC  Section  11.51.070  "Temporary  Use  Perinit,"  temporary  use  permits  are processed
  administratively  to "allow  for short-term  activities  that warrant  individual  consideration  and are
  acceptable  because  of  their  temporary,  short-term  nature."  SGMC  Section  11.51.070  (A)
  "Temporary  Uses,"  also notes that the "provisions  of this section  shall regulate  all special  events,
  and temporary  land uses as pen'nitted  by Table  11.21-3,  11.21-4,  or 11.21-5,  as applicable  to the
  zone, or as detennined  by the director."  SGMC  Section  11.51.010  (B) lists "Mandatory  Approval
  Conditions"  for temporary  use permits,  wherein  there are "limits  on the maximum  duration  will
  be specified  in the permit,  and shall not exceed  three days in a row,  or ten working  days in any
  calendar  year."

  Original  Issuance  of the TUP was Done in Error,  and Renewal  of the TUP is not authorized  by the
  SGMC.  Based  on limitations  imposed  by the South  Gate Municipal  Code upon  the issuance  of
  Temporary  Use Peri'nits  as set forth  hereinabove,  and notwithstanding  the language  contained
  within  TUP2020-01,  the Director  of Cornrnunity  Development  was prohibited  from  granting  an
  extension  of TUP2020-01.  The Plaru'iing  Comt'nission  was similarly  prohibited  from  granting  an
  extension  of TUP2020-01  for similar  reasons  and upheld  the Director's  Determination.

  Temporary  Use Permit  2020-01  should  never have been issued in the first place for the purported
  use (which  is prohibited  within  the IF Zone)  nor for the duration  set forth therein,  since it purported
  to authorize  the subject  use for one year (with  possible  extensions  for a total  of 5 years from  the

we respectfully  request that the City acknowledge  that each of these conditions have
been met to the extent possible.

  3.  Terminatinq  the Leqal  Nonconforminq  Use Violates  the Doctrine  of
  Equitable  Estoppel

  The Doctrine of Equitable Estoppel was designed to promote fair and equitable
business transactions.  The doctrine is based on the principle that a party who has
made a promise should be held accountable  for it where reliance on the agreement  was
reasonable,  and enforcement  of the agreement  is necessary to avoid injustice.
Drennan v. StarPaving  Co. (1958) 51 Cal.2d 409, 412-413:  Garcia v World Sav. &
LoanAssn. (2010) 183 Cal.App.4th 10311037.  Here, Fleet Yards only agreed to the
TUP as a demonstration  of good faith and willingness  to work with the City regarding its
vision for the community.  Based on communications  from City staff on July 8, 2020, in
addition to the plain language of the TUP, the City was to consider additional extensions
of the TOP in addition to the initial five-year term. In addition, both AEP and Fleet Yards
agreed to the TUP as a measure of good faith and willingness  to work with the City. It is
inequitable for the City to renege on this agreement.  AEP forwent multiple lucrative
opportunities  to sell the Property in reliance on the City's communications  and the
reasonable  expectation  that the City's permits, licenses, and representations  are
consistent notwithstanding  changes in staff, changes in departmental  priorities, and
unilateral changes to the zoning code. If the City does not honor its prior commitments,
both AEP and Fleet Yards will suffer substantial financial harm. In addition, this
inconsistency  in City policies discourages  investment  in our community  and is a
substantial deviation from the City's treatment of similarly situated legacy businesses

  4.  Conclusion

  For the reasons stated above, the equitable path forward is to acknowledge  truck
trailer storage on the Property as a preserved,  legal nonconforming  use in light of the
substantial  evidence supporting  this finding, and the requirements  of the General Plan.
In the alternative,  we respectfully  request that the City reverse the Director's denial of
the TUP extension.  We understand  that the City's position is that the TUP was issued in
error. However, where, as here, immediately  terminating  the TLIP causes substantial
harm to the community,  and there is substantial  evidence supporting  that the use is
legal and nonconforming,  we urge you to use this opportunity  to make it right. As a
further demonstration  of good faith and willingness  to work together, we respectfully
request the City share any documentation  indicating that the truck trailer storage is not
authorized pursuant to the legacy operations  on the Property, and procedures  for
obtaining a business permit zoning dearance  where, as here, the use is legal
nonconforming.

As the City has repeatedly advised AEP and Fleet Yards, the TUP was initially issued in error, because it
purported to allow a "temporary" use of the Premises for a period of at least one year and possibly as many as
five years, far in excess of the limited duration mandated by the Zoning Code. Temporary use permits, as the
name implies, are intended to allow only short-term uses of land. Specifically, Section 11.51.070 of the Zoning
Code states that the maximum duration of a temporary use permit shall not exceed three days in a row or ten
days in any calendar year. It is unfortunate that the TUP was erroneously issued in 2020 for a much longer one-
year period and erroneously renewed in 2021 for an additional one-year period. But those earlier errors do not
entitle AEP to further extensions of the TUP for periods far in excess of the maximum durations authorized  by
the Zoning Code. Simply put, there is no authority in the Zoning Code for issuing or renewing a temporary  use
permit for any period longer than three consecutive days or ten days in any calendar year.

Furthermore, the original issuance of the TUP in violation of the Zoning Code also meant that the City was not
required to grant AEP a hearing on the matter of renewing the TUP. Again, as publicly stated by the City's legal
counsel at the Planning Commission meeting, the City granted that hearing aS a matter Of courtesy - something
that was also explained to AEP in the course of the May 2 meeting. No hearing was required because no
decision by the Planning Commission could have resulted in validation and extension of the TUP. Section
11.51.020 of the Zoning Code states that any permit conflicting with the provisions of the Zoning Code "shall be
null and void." Both the TUP and the requested one-year extension conflict with the provisions of the Zoning

History of Zoning and Land Use of Subiect Property
As early as 1961, the Subject Property was designated as being  within  a Heavy  Manufacturing
("M-3")  Zone,

Based  upon  a review  of public  records  and documents  submitted  by AEP,  the Site was used by
Jack Engel  & Company  (hereinafter,  "JECO")  and/or AEP for ametal  processing/recycling  facility
from  as early as 1973 until  approximately  March  2020.  During  that time,  the site was developed
with a single-story  industrial  structure  used for the recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO  and/or
AEP.

The metal  recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO  and/or  AEP  included,  but was not limited  to,
the delivery  of scrap metal product  to the Site inside  of truck  trailers  - which  would  remain  on site
for up to several  months  while  the scrap metal  was sorted  and processed  on-site  and prepared  for

In 1988, the City amended its Zoning Code, in part, to require a Conditional Use Permit for

2323, which further amended the Zoning Code and changed the zoning classification of the Subject
Property  to Industrial Flex ("IF") Zone.

Pursuant to the Section 11.21.030 and Table 11.21-3 of the amended Zoning Code, recycling
facilities require a Conditional Use Permit - however, the recycling operations at the Subject

ANALYSIS:

Appeal  of Director's  Determination
On January  21, 2025,  the City  sent a Director's  Deterinination  and Noncompliance  Notification
letter  to the applicant  indicating  the legal,  nonconfon'ning  use of the Subject  Property  for metal
processing  and/or  recycling  activities  - including  the integral  truck  trailer  storage  component  of
those activities  - has been determined  to be abandoned  and can no longer  be conducted  at the Site
unless  otherwise  in confon'nity  to all current  laws  and regulations  of the City  (and  applicable
governmental  agencies).  Furthermore,  based  on staff's  research  and information  provided  by
Somos,  the  use  of  the  Site  for  truck  trailer  storage  as a principal  use unrelated  to  metal
processing/recycling  activities  is not  a legal,  nonconforming  use -  and,  as such,  must  be
iini'nediately  terminated.

On  February  6,  2025,  the  applicant  filed  an  appeal  requesting  the  Planning  Commission
challenging  the Director's  determination  based on the following  grounds:

1.  The Director's  Determination  is unsupported  by the South  Gate Municipal  Code  (SGMC)
  purportedly  due to the Director's  differentiation  between  an ancillary  and primary  use, that the
  immediate  termination  of a legal,  nonconforming  use is inconsistent  with  the SGMC  and
  General  Plan, and the Determination  violates  procedural  requirements;
2.  Substantive  and procedural  due process  concerns;  and
3. Termination of a legal, nonconforming use is a defacto regulatory taking; and,
4.  The City's  failure  to comply  with  the California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA),  Public
  Resources  Code Section  21000,  et seq.

Truck  Storage/Teri'ninal  Use: AEP  and its tenant  have been using  the subject  property  to store
trucks,  truck-trailers,  and storage  containers  Under  the SGMC,  this use is defined  as "truck
storage/terminal"  use which,  pursuant  to the SGMC  Section  11.60.230  "T"  definitions,  "means
indoor  or outdoor  site for  freight,  truck  terminals,  truck  storage  yards,  or similar  cornrnercial
facilities."

SGMC  Prohibits  that Use at 8530 Alameda  Street:  The subject  property  is zoned  Industrial  Flex
(IF). Table  11.21-3,  under  SGMC  Section  11.21.030  "Land  use permissions  tables,"  lists allowed
land uses within  the IF zone. Truck  storage/terminal  use is not listed  on that Table  as an allowed
use within  the IF zone.  SGMC  Section  11.21.020  notes that "Any  land use that is not specifically
listed  in the land use tables  for the applicable  zone shall not be allowed  or permitted  within  the

issues of contention  are (i) whether  the legal, nonconforming  recycling/metal  processing  activities

  In response  to the appellant's  arguments  set forth  in the Request  for Appeal,  Staff  submits  the

  ASSERTION:  The  Director's  Determination  is unsupported  by the South  Gate  Municipal
  Code.
  The  appellant  first  argues  that  the  Director  failed  to make  a determination  that  the  legal,
  nonconforming  use is "wholly  discontinued  or abandoned  for a continuous  period  of two calendar
  years"  as required  by SGMC  11.55.040(D).  The Director,  however,  correctly  deten'nined  that the
  legal,  nonconforming  recycling/metal  processing  use at the site was wholly  discontinued  and/or
  abandoned  - as evidenced  by the cessation  of all activities  associated  with  the recycling/metal
  processing  activities  in  or around  2020,  including  the  demolition  of the  structure  that  was
  previously  utilized  for such activities.  Contrary  to the appellant's  contention,  the Director  did not
  distinguish  between  primary  and  ancillary  legal,  non-conforming  uses.  Rather,  the  Director
  accepted  the appellants  assertion  that the storage  of truck  trailers  at the site was an "integral  part
  of metal  processing  operations,"  however,  the Director  did determine  that the truck  trailer  storage
  was  only  done  as part  of the recycling/metal  processing  activities  while  those  activities  were
  occurring.  The Director  correctly  determined  that the current  use of the site for truck trailer  storage
  only  is NOT  a continuation  of the use of the trucks  for the recycling/metal  processing  activities,
  and, is, in fact, a wholly  new use.

  The appellant  also argues that the irnrnediate  termination  of the truck  trailer  storage is inconsistent
  with the South Gate Municipal  Code and the General  Plan - which  the appellant  contends  promotes
  a more  gradual  transition  to a confornning  use.  However,  the appellant  fails  to recognize  that it
  was the appellant's  abandonment  of the recycling/metal  processing  activities  formore  than 2 years
  that resulted  in the termination  of its legal, nonconforming  rights  - and not any action  by the City.
  The City's  requirement  that the legal,  nonconforming  use be terminated  for 2 continuous  years
  does, in fact, provide  for a gradual  transition  - but the appellant  failed  to utilize  those 2 years to
  make  a transition  to a confornning  use.  Instead,  the appellant  transitioned  to using  the subject
  property  for the prohibited  truck  trailer  storage use.

  The  appellant  further  mistakenly  argues  that  the Director  failed  to make  findings  required  by
  Section  11.55.040(D)  of the municipal  code.  Specifically,  the appellant  argues that the Director
  failed  to consider  and make  a determination  regarding  (i) the property  owner's  intent;  (ii)  the
  presence  or absence  of personal  property  associated  with  the legal,  nonconforming  use;  (iii)
  presence  or absence  of furnishings,  equipment,  and other  property  associated  with  the use; and,
  (iv) continuity  of utility  service  to the property.

  The appellant  incorrectly  interprets  SGMC  §11.55.040(D).  Pursuant  to SGMC  §11.55.040(D)(1),
  in  order  to  determine  whether  a  property  owner  has  abandoned/discontinued  a  legal,
  nonconforming  use, the Director  is required  to determine  the "apparent  intent  of the owner  to
  discontinue  use of the nonconforming  structure  is apparent,  as determined  by  the  director"
  (emphasis  added).  This  particular  requirement,  however,  is  applicable  to  the  intent  to
  discontinue/abandon  anonconforming  structure  - and not the owner's  intent  to discontinue  a legal,
  nonconforming  use. That being said, the Director  determined  that the structure  previously  existing

  for recycling/metal  processing  activities  has been abandoned/discontinued  for more than 2 years.

  The appellant  contends  that the manner  in which  the City  has handled  requests  from  appellant's

  no longer  in the possession  of the City.  [Business  licenses  are issued to business  operators  - and

  ASSERTION:  Termination  of the legal nonconforming  use is a de facto regulatory  taking.
  The appellant  contends  that the changes  to the City's  Zoning  laws and General  Plan amount  to a
  regulatory  taking  because  of the limited  uses allowed  at the subject  property.  However,  the City

  recycling/metal  processing  activities  - and it is the Director's  determination  that the truck  trailer

  from  the  Termination  of  the  Existing  Land  Use  m Favor  of  alternative  Land  Uses
  Inconsistent  with  the Requirements  of CEQA.
  The appellant  incorrectly  asserts that the City's  termination  of the legal, nonconforming  use of the

In  accordance  with  the  California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA),  the  Director's

The Planning  Commission's  determination  on the termination  of the legal,  non-conforming  use of
the  subject  property  is not  subject  to California  Environmental  Quality  Act  (CEQA)  review
because  it is not  an "approval"  as defined  in California  Code  of Regulations,  Title  14,  Section
15352,  but rather  a determination  of whether  a use must terminate  at a site, and therefore  does not
commit  the City  to any definite  course  of action  regarding  new  uses or changes  to the approved
use of the subject  property.  Furthermore,  CEQA  does not apply  to projects  which  a public  agency
rejects  or disapproves  pursuant  to Section  1 5270(a).

BACKGROUND
This  is an appeal  by the applicant,  Somos  Law  Group  ("Somos"),  on behalf  of the property  owner,
Alameda  Engle  Properties,  LLC  ("AEP"  represented  by Jason Engle),  for  a 6.78-acre  property
located  at 8530  Alameda  Street.  Somos  is appealing  the Director  of Community  Development's
decision  that the legal,  nonconforming  use for metal  processing  and/or  recycling  activities  at the
subject  property  has been abandoned  and can no longer  be conducted,  and the use of the site for
truck  trailer  storage  as a principal  use unrelated  to metal  processing/recycling  activities  is not a
legal,  nonconforming  use and must be immediately  terminated.  Somos  is also requesting  to change
the zoning  of the subject  property  from  IF (Industrial  Flex)  to M3  (Heavy  Manufacturing)  and
remove  the subject  property  from  the South  Gate  College  District  as shown  in the Community
Design  Element  of the General  Plan.

It should  be noted  that AEP  also owns  the abutting  2.9-acre  site to the north  at 8440  S. Alameda
Street,  which  is located  outside  of the City  and in the County  of Los  Angeles.  Access  to both
properties  is via a driveway  from  Alameda  Street to the property  at 8440  S. Alameda  Street.  This
property  is also being  used for truck  trailer  storage  and according  to County  staff,  a conditional
use permit  (CUP)  is currently  being  processed.

History  of Zoning  and  Land  Use of Subject  Property
As early  as 1961,  the Subject  Property  was designated  as being  within  a Heavy  Manufacturing
("M-3")  Zone.

Pursuant  to the Section  11.21.030  and Table  11.21-3  of the amended  Zoning  Code,  recycling
facilities  require  a Conditional  Use Permit  - however,  the recycling  operations  at the Subject
Property  were deemed  to be a legal,  nonconforming  land use that was allowed  to continue  in
accordance  with  SGMC  Chapter  11.55 ("Nonconforming  Uses and Buildings").

According  to public  records and information  submitted  by AEP and/or its representatives,  all metal
recycling  operations  ceased in or around  March  2020 and are no longer  being  conducted  at the
Site.

AEP has confirmed  that around March  2020, Fleet Yards, Inc. commenced  utilizing  the Site solely
for the storage of truck trailers  and/or  containers  as a principal  use. Moreover,  the structure  that
was previously  utilized  to conduct  the metal recycling  at the Site was demolished.

In July 2020, the City  approved  Fleet Yards,  Inc.'s  application  for a Temporary  Use Permit  and
issued TUP2020-01,  authorizing  the use of the Subject Property  for "truck  trailer  storage for a one-

of approval".  TUP2020-01  expired  on July 16, 2021, without  a timely  request for renewal  from
Fleet Yards, Inc.

In December  2022, the Director  advised  Fleet Yards,  Inc. that several  conditions  of approval  of
the TUP had not been adhered to, and, moreover,  that the TUP was ineligible  for renewal  as SGMC

ANALYSIS:

Appeal  of Director's  Determination
On January  21, 2025, the City sent a Director's  Determination  and Noncompliance  Notification
letter to the applicant  indicating  the legal, nonconforming  use of the Subject  Property  for metal
processing  and/or  recycling  activities  - including  the integral  truck  trailer  storage component  of
those activities  - has been determined  to be abandoned  and can no longer be conducted  at the Site
unless  otherwise  in conformity  to all current  laws and regulations  of the City  (and applicable
governmental  agencies).  Furthermore,  based on staff's  research  and information  provided  by
Somos,  the use of the  Site  for  truck  trailer  storage  as a principal  use unrelated  to metal
processing/recycling  activities  is not  a legal,  nonconforming  use -  and,  as such,  must  be
immediately  terminated.

On  February  6, 2025,  the  applicant  filed  an appeal  requesting  the  Planning  Commission
challenging  the Director's  determination  based  on  the following  grounds:

1.  The Director's  Determinatton  is unsupported  by the South  Gate Municipal  Code (SGMC)
  purportedly  due to the Director's  differentiation  between  an ancillary  and primary  use, that the
  immediate  termination  of a legal,  nonconforming  use is inconsistent  with  the SGMC  and
  General  Plan, and the Determination  violates  procedural  requirements;
2.  Substantive  and procedural  due process concerns;  and
3. Termination of a legal, nonconforming use is a defacto regulatory taking; and,
4.  The City's  failure  to comply  with  the California  Environmental  Quality  Act (CEQA),  Public
  Resources  Code Section 21000,  et seq.

Truck  Storage/Terminal  Use: AEP  and its tenant  have been using  the subject  property  to store
trucks,  truck-trailers,  and storage  containers.  Under  the SGMC,  this use is defined  as "truck
storage/terminal"  use which,  pursuant  to the SGMC  Section  11.60.230  "T"  definitions,  "means
indoor  or outdoor  site for freight,  truck  terminals,  truck  storage  yards,  or similar  commercial
facilities."

SGMC  Prohibits  that Use at 8530 Alameda  Street:  The subject property  is zoned Industrial  Flex
(IF). Table 11.21-3,  under SGMC  Section  11.21.030  "Land  use permissions  tables,"  lists allowed
land uses within  the IF zone. Truck  storage/terminal  use is not listed on that Table as an allowed

  Analysis

SGMC Chapter 11.55 ("Nonconforming  Uses and Buildings")  provides  regulations
governing the establishment,  maintenance,  and continuance  of uses, structures, and
parcels that were lawfully established  but no longer conform to current City laws and
regu!ations  (commonly  called "legal, nonconforming"  or "nonconforming"  uses and
buildings).  It further provides  regulations  for repair, maintenance,  alterations,  and
expansions  of legal, nonconforming  buildings and uses - as well as grounds and
procedures for the termination of legal, nonconforming  uses and buildings.

The person claiming the existence  of a nonconforming  building or use has the burden  of
proof with regard to that claim.3

  II.  Analysis

  a.  The Director's  Determination  is Unsupported  by the SGMC

  The Code Does  not Allow the Director  to Differentiate  Ancillary  from
  Primary Uses

  The SGMC unequivocally  requires protection for "all nonconforming  buildings or
uses, including outdoor activities such as product storage or parking."2 The SGMC
specifically  protects all parts of a legal nonconforming  use. Before a use or any part of
a use can be terminated  for abandonment  or discontinuation,  the Director must make
substantiated  findings that the use is "whollydiscontinued  orabandonedfor  a
continuous  period of two calendar years."3 The Director cannot make such findings
based on the documentation  submitted  to the City. In addition, the City must treat "an
existing use of any part of a building or property...  to be an existing use throughout  that
building or property, including outdoor activities.""  This language clarifies that once a
use is legally established,  it is legally established for the entirety of the property -
indicating that separating  parts of a property or parts of a use are inappropriate  in a
legal nonconforming  use analysis. Here, the truck trailer and container  use has been a
continuous  use on the property since the metal recycling operations  began in 1973.
This has been documented  at length in letters and materials submitted to the City on
April 27, 2023, May 2, 2023, May 16, 2023, and August 17, 2023. On August 17, 2023,
our office provided copies of all available business licenses for the property.  Any
licenses that were not available were requested  from the City, but not provided. The
licenses issued to Jack Engle and Company  ("JECO") for the Property span between
2015 and 2018, and specifically  acknowledge  that "outdoor  storage" as an authorized
use on the site. There is no delineation  between primary and ancillary uses on the
permits.  In addition, our office provided licenses issued to Fleet Yards that specifically
acknowledge  a special permit for "outdoor  storage."  As you know, the City must

made a promise should be held accountable for it where reliance on the agreement was
reasonable, and enforcement  of the agreement is necessary to avoid injustice.
Drennan v. Star Paving CO. (1958) 51 Cal.2d 409, 4'l2-4"l3; Garcia v. t/Ubrld Sav &

opportunities  to sell the Property in reliance on the City's communications  and the

unilateral changes to the zoning code. If the City does not honor its prior commitments,

  The Doctrine of Equitable Estoppel was designed to promote fair and equitable
business transactions.  The doctrine is based on the principle that a party who has
made a promise should be held accountable for it where reliance on the agreement was
reasonable,  and enforcement  of the agreement is necessary to avoid injustice.
Drennan v. StarPaving  Co. (1958) 51 Cal2d 409, 412-413; Garcia v. Worrd Sav &
Loein Assn. (2010)183 Cal.App.4th 10311037. Here, Fleet Yards only agreed to the
TuP as a demonstration of good faith and willingness to work with the City regarding its
vision for the community.  Based on communications  from City sta'ff on July 8, 2020, in
addition to the plain language of the TUP, the City was to consider additional extensions

reasonable expectation that the City's permits, licenses, and representations  are

unilateratchangestothezoningcode.  lftheCitydoesnothonoritspriorcommitments,

furnishings equipment, or personal property have been removed, (iii) whether the use
has been discontinued  for a period of two years, (iv) whether there is an active business
license and State Board of Equalization  permit, and (v) whether there are active utilities
accounts, including electricity, gas, water, and waste collection.29

 Past/Proposed Use of Pro'perty is as a "Truck Storaze/Terminal":  Applicant and its tenant have been using the

History  of Zoning  and Land  Use of Subject  Property
As early  as 1961,  the Subject  Property  was designated  as being  within  a Heavy  Manufacturing
("M-3")  Zone.

Based  upon  a review  of public  records  and documents  submitted  by AEP,  the Site was used by
Jack Engel  & Company  (hereina:[ter,  "JECO")  and/or  AEP for ametal  processing/recycling  facility

AS13772.0860893  4909-8288-0805vl
  413
  3
 from  as early  as 1973  until  approximately  March  2020.  During  that time,  the site was developed
with  a single-story  industrial  structure  used for the recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO  and/or
AEP.

The metal  recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO  and/or  AEP  included,  but was not limited  to,
the delivery  of scrap metal product  to the Site inside  of truck  trailers  - which  would  remain  on site
for up to several  months  while  the scrap metal  was sorted and processed  on-site  and prepared  for
shipment  to a final  off-site  destination.
In 1988,  the City  amended  its Zoning  Code,  in part,  to require  a Conditional  Use  Permit  for
recycling  facilities.  Thereafter,  on or about April  28, 2015,  the City  Council  adopted  Ordinance
2323, which  'further  amended  the Zoning  Code and changed  the zoning  classification  of the Subject
Property  to Industrial  Flex  ("IF")  Zone.

AEP has confirmed  that around  March  2020, Fleet Yards,  Inc. commenced  utilizing  the Site solely
for the storage  of truck  trailers  and/or  containers  as a principal  use.  Moreover,  the structure  that
was previously  utilized  to conduct  the metal recycling  at the Site was demolished.

ANALYSIS:

Zoning  Map  Amendment  and General  Plan  Amendment
The applicant  is requesting  to change  the zoning  of the property  at 8530 Alameda  Street from  IF
to M3  and remove  the subject  propcrty  from  the South  Gate  College  District  as shown  in the
Community  Design  Element  of the General  Plan.  The request  is to accommodate  Fleet  Yards,
Inc.'s  operation  as a truck  storage/ternninal  facility.

Around  2015,  the City  rezoned  properties  in the area from  M3  to IF. This  was to accommodate
future  growth  of the East Los Angeles  Cornrnunity  College  ("ELACC")  within  the South  Gate
College  District  as described  in the Community  Design  Element  of the City's  General  Plan.  The
subject  property  is included  in the South Gate College  District  as part of sub-area  I (portions  north
of Firestone  Boulevard  and east of Alameda  Street).  ELACC  anticipates  a largely  expanded
campus  complex  that would  include  adaptive  reuse of nearby  industrial  facilities  along  Firestone
Boulevard.  Changing  the zone to M3 would  be contrary  to the vision  and policies  of the General

The IF zone allows  certain  residential  uses to be developed  and changing  the zoning  to M3 would
preclude  potential  new housing  development,  which  is contrary  to the City's  Housing  Element  and
the Statewide  regional  housing  needs.  Moreover,  such  rezoning  would  remove  509 potential

within  180 days, to identify  new suitable  housing  locations  within  the City  to replace  some or all
of the lost  locations.  Furthermore,  uses such  as recreation,  education,  public  assembly,  parks,
plazas,  and open space, which  are allowed  in the IF zone would  be prohibited  in the M3 zone.  For
all of those  reasons,  as such,  staff  recommends  the Planning  Commission  reject  the proposed

The applicant,  Somos Law  Group  ("Somos"),  on behalf  of the property  owner,  Alameda  Engle

History  of Zoning  and Land  Use of Subject  Property
As early as 1961,  the Subject  Property  was designated  as being within  a Heavy  Manufacturing
("M-3")  Zone.

Based upon a review  of public  records  and documents  submitted  by AEP, the Site was used by
Jack Engel & Company  (hereinafter,  "JECO")  and/or AEP for a metal processing/recycling  facility
from  as early as 1973 until  approximately  March  2020.  During  that time, the site was developed
with a single-story  industrial  structure  used for the recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO and/or
AEP.

The metal recycling  operations  conducted  by JECO and/or AEP included,  but was not limited  to,
the delivery  of scrap metal product  to the Site inside of truck trailers  - which  would  remain  on  site
for up to several months while the scrap metal was sorted and processed  on-site,  and prepared  for
shipment to a final off-site destination.

In 1988,  the City  amended  its Zoning  Code,  in part, to require  a Conditional  Use Permit  for
recycling  facilities.  Thereafter,  on or about April  28, 2015, the City Council  adopted  Ordinance
2323, which further amended the Zoning  Code and changed the zoning classification  ofthe  Subject
Property to Industrial Flex ("IF") Zone.

AEP has confirmed  that around March  2020, Fleet Yards, Inc. commenced  utilizing  the Site solely
for the storage of truck trailers  and/or  containers  as a principal  use. Moreover,  the structure  that
was previously  utilized  to conduct  the metal recycling  at the Site was demolished.

The Facts: How We Got Here

For decades,8530 Alameda Streetwas home to a metal processing and recycling facility, Even
after zoning changes in 2015, the City allowed the business to continue under tegal
nonconforming status, showing its wi[lingness to work with )ong-standing businesses and
provide flexibi(ity for property owners.

However, that nonconforming status required renewal and in 2020, the property owner failed to
submit that renewal. As a result, the legal protection for that prior use expired, and the site
became subject to the current Industrial Flex (IF) zoning, which does not allow truck trailer
storage.

Despite this, the site has continued to be used Fortruck trailer storage, an operation that was
never separately recognized as a legal nonconforming use. The City is now requiring
compliance with existing zoning, which is a necessary and standard enforcement action.

South Gate's Approach Has Been Fair and Consistent

The City of South Gate has a proven history of working with its business community, and this
case is no exception. The fact that the previous nonconforming use was allowed to continue for
nearly five years after the zoning change shows that the City was not looking to push
businesses out but instead offered reasonable opportunities to transition.

 Addressing Arguments Against the City's Decision

therefore should still qualify under the origina( nonconforming status. However, the key issue is
that nonconForming use protections do not extend indefinitely without proper renewal.

  -  The original nonconforming status applied specifically to metal processing, not to
truck storage as a separate business.

  -  Once metal processing ceased and the structure was demolished, the truck
storage became an independent operation-not  a continuation of the original use.

  -  Under South Gate's current zoning regulations, truck trailer storage is not a
permitted use in the IF zone.

The City is not changing the rutes or targeting this specific business. If noncomp)iant operations
were allowed to continue indefinitefy without proper renewal, it would undermine the entire
purpose  of zoning Iaws.

who failed to take the necessary steps to maintain theirlegal standing. It is misleading and

Application

move forward in the recruitment process. Prior security guard and customer service experience
are highly recommended  and/or required depending on the scope of the role.

In-person  Interview
Interviews are conducted by the company's senior management  team to ensure  applicants  meet
the skills and qualifications required to perform the role.

References,  Background  Check,  and Offer
 Once a candidate has been selected for the position, his or her professional  references are
contacted. We also verify candidates' employment  history, including requesting information on
job performance,  strengths, and weaknesses.  An offer is extended to successful candidates.

On-boarding  & Placement

and completion of the new hire package which includes the 1-9 verification and a copy of key
policies. The employee will be placed in an account in which his/her experience and knowledge
will fulfill the client's needs and expectations.

 AJS!ALYSIS:  The  proposed  Agreement  for  the  construction  of  the  Residential  Resurfacing
 Project  was procured  through  a competitive  bidding  process.  The bid documents  required  bidders
 to submit  both  a Base Bid  and an Additive  Bid,  and indicated  that the lowest  bidder  was to be
 determined  solely  based  on the  Base  Bid  amount.  Sequel  Contractors  submitted  the  lowest

 the  bids  received  is provided  in  the  table  on the  next  page,  with  the  detailed  bid  analysis
 available  in Attachment  "C."  Staff  recommends  awarding  the contract  to Sequel  Contractors  in
 the amount  of $3,638,773.  This  contract  amount  includes  both the Base Bid and the Additive  Bid
 amounts.  The street improvements  and costs are listed  in the suminary  table on the next page.

 The  primary  purpose  of the project  is to rehabilitate  residential  streets:  however,  the project
 includes  street  improvements  originally  planned  for construction  on other  projects,  such as the
 reconstruction  of ADA  ramps  on Long  Beach  Blvd.  Instead  of processing  costly  change  orders
 to fund  and construct  these improvements,  they were bid as a part of the Residential  Resurfacing

  BACKGROUND:  The Fiscal  Year  2024/25  Capital  Improvement  Program  (FY  2024/25  CIP)
  allocates  funding  to the Citywide  Residential  Resurfacing,  Phase IV,  Project  and the Citywide
  Sidewalk  Improvements,  Phase X, Project.  These  projects  aim to rehabilitate  street  pavements,
  and repair  sidewalks  on residential  streets.  Staff  consolidated  both  of these projects  under  the
  Residential  Resurfacing  Project  to  construct  them  concurrently.  This  approach  ensures:  (1)
  simultaneous  resolution  of  pavement  and  sidewalk  conditions,  (2)  reduced  disruption  for
  residents  and motorists  by limiting  repeated  construction  activities,  (3) enhanced  efficiency  in
  project  management,  and  (4)  greater  competitiveness  and  cost-effectiveness.  That  said  the
  proposed  Agreement  provides  for the construction  of both projects.

  The proposed  Agreement  was procured  through  a competitive  bidding  process.  On March  20,
  2025,  staff publicly  advertised  a Notice  Inviting  Bids  in the Daily  Journal,  on the City's  website,
  and via PlanetBids.  On April  17, 2025,  the City  Clerk  received  and publicly  opened  four  bids.
  Following  a bid evaluation,  Sequel  was determined  to be the lowest  responsible  and responsive
  bidder.  Sequel  submitted  a total  bid  amount  of $3,638,773,  which  included  the Base  Bid  and
  Additive  Bid.  A surnrnary  of the bids received  is provided  below.

Sequel  possesses  the demonstrated  capacity,  resources,  and experience  necessary  to successfully
complete  the work  described  in the proposed  Agreement.  They  are based in Santa Fe Springs,
California,  and  have  successfully  operated  for  30  years.  Sequel  has  completed  numerous
construction  projects  for  the  City  of  South  Gate,  including  the recently  finished  Residential
Resurfacing  Projects  Phases I through  III,  Tweedy  Mile  and Garfield  Complete  Streets,  and the
Long  Beach  Blvd  Street  Improvements.  Regardless  of  staf'f's  experience  with  Sequel,  staff
contacted  references  and they provided  positive  feedback  on their performance.

Pursuant  to  the  guidelines  of  the  California  Environinental  Quality  Act  ("CEQA"),  the
Residential  Resurfacing  Project  is categorically  exempt  under  Title  14 of the California  Code of
Regulations,  Section  15301.  Specifically,  it qualifies  for exemption  under  Section  15301  Class
(c), which  covers  existing  highways  and streets,  sidewalks,  gutters,  bicycle  and pedestrian  trails,
and  similar  existing  facilities,  including  road  grading  perforined  for  public  safety  purposes.
Additionally,  the  project  has been  determined  categorically  excluded  under  Section  326  of
amended  Chapter  3 of Title  23, United  States Code (23 U.S.C.  § 326), confirming  that it does not
significantly  impact  the  environment  as defined  by  the National  Environmental  Policy  Act
("NEP A").

Construction  is expected  to begin  in May  2025 and be completed  in November  2025.

SUBJECT:  CONSIDER  ADOPTION  OF  RESOLUTION  MAKING  CERT  AIN  FINDINGS
FOR  AN  EXCEPTION  TO  THE  180-DAY  WAIT  PERIOD  PURSUANT  TO  CALIFORNIA
GOVERNMENT  CODE  SECTIONS  7522.56  AND  21221

PURPOSE:  The  Pension  Reform  Act  of  2012  prohibits  employers  from  hiring  retired  annuitants
within  180 days of their  retirement.  However,  subsequent  legislation  provides  for an exception  to the
180-day  wait  period  under  specific  conditions,  i.e.,  the  California  Public  Employees'  Retirement
System  (CalPERS)  requires  the City  Council  adopt  a resolution  to allow  for an exception  to the 180-
day wait period  to hire a retired  employee  for temporary,  part-time  employment  during  the wait period.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  City  Council  is requested  to consider  adoption  of a Resolution
making  certain  findings  that  allow  a recently  retired  Director  of Finance  to be hired  for  temporary,
part-time  employment  with  the City  of South  Gate commencing  within  the 180-day  wait  period  from
his retirement  from  the City  of South Pasadena.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The making  of certain  findings  for an exception  to the 180-day  wait  period  will
require  no additional  appropriations  for  Fiscal  Year  2024/25  due to salary  savings  from  the Senior
Accountant,  Deputy  Director  of Finance,  and the Budget  & Finance  Manager  positions  being  vacant  in
the Administrative  Services  Department  will  be used to cover the salary  cost for this retired  aru'iuitant.

ANALYSIS:  None.

BACKGROUND:  Certified  Public  Accountant  John Downs  (hereinafter  "Downs")  retired  from  the
City  of South Pasadena  as its Director  of Finance  effective  December  31, 2024, with  approximately  30
years  of experience  in finance  and accounting.  He has extensive  experience  in municipal  accounting
and financing,  as well  as budget  preparation  and oversight.

On or about  January  21, 2025,  the City's  Deputy  Director  of Finance  announced  her resignation  to
return  to her previous  employer,  and,  on January  27,  2025,  the  City's  Director  of Administrative
Services  announced  her resignation  to pursue  an opportunity  elsewhere.  As  a result  of these  two
resignations  and the vacancy  of the Budget  & Finance  Manager  position,  the Administrative  Services
Department  did  not  have  a functional  manager.  Accordingly,  the  City  hired  retired  annuitant  Mr.
Downs  into  an Interim  Director  of  Administrative  Services  to  lead  the  Administrative  Services
Department  as the City recruited  for a regular,  permanent  Director  of Administrative  Services.

  1

  543
 In addition  to Mr.  Downs  functioning  as the department's  interim  head and under  the direction  of the
City  Manager,  he was assigned  to chair  the City's  budget  preparation  for Fiscal  Year  2025/26,  which
includes  revenue  projections  and determination  of fund  balances  for general  and special  funds.  The
budget  process  takes approximately  four  months  to complete  and began  in March  2025.  During  Mr.
Downs  service  as the  City's  Interim  Director  of  Administrative  Services,  the  City  conducted  a
successful  recruitment  for  a permanent  Director  of Administrative  Services,  Mr.  Luis  Frausto,  who
began  his employment  on Monday,  May  12, 2025.  Because  Mr.  Downs  may  no longer  serve in the
capacity  of the Interim  Director  of Administrative  Services  once Mr.  Frausto  began  his employment,
he may only continue  in the capacity  of providing  "extra  help"  to the City  as a retired  annuitant.

Prior  to Mr. Downs'  service  as the City's  Interim  Director  of Administrative  Services,  he worked  as a
consultant  approximately  10 years  ago. At  that  time,  Mr.  Downs  served  as the  functional  Deputy
Finance  Director  for almost  four  years, wherein  he became  familiar  with  the City's  budgets,  spending
patterns,  forecasting  needs,  and can identify  cost-saving  opportunities  unique  to the City.  Because  of
his  experience,  he has the  expertise  prioritizing  how  resources  and personnel  should  be allocated
across different  departments,  projects,  and/or  initiatives.  As the Interim  Director,  Mr.  Downs,  provided
important  input  in the City's  upcoming  fiscal  budget,  it is crucial  to have him continue  is work  with  the
City to perfon'n  special  projects  and work  related  to this budgetary  process  and other responsibilities  of
the department.  a

Pursuant  to California  Government  Code Fp7522.56(b),  "[a]  retired  person  shall not serve, be employed
by, or be employed  through  a contract  directly  by a public  employer  in the same public  retirement
system  from  which  the retiree  received  the benefit  without  reinstatement  from  retirement,  except  as
permitted  by this  section."  California  Governrnent  Code  Fp 7522.56(c),  then  provides  the following
exception:  "A  retired  person  may  serve  without  reinstatement  or loss,  or internuption  of benefits
provided  by [CalPERS]  upon  appointment  by the appointing  power  of a public  employer  either  during
an emergency  to prevent  stoppage  of public  business  or because  the retired  person  has specialized
skills needed in performing work of a limited duration." California Government Code E>7522.56(f)(1)
provides:  "A  retired  person  shall not be eligible  to be employed  pursuant  to this section  for a period  of
180  days  following  the  date  of  retirement  unless...  [t]he  employer  certifies  the  nature  of  the
employment  and the appointment  is necessary  to fill  a critically  needed  position  before  180 days have
passed  and the appointment  has been  approved  by the governing  body  of the employer  in a public
meeting.  The  appointment  may  not be placed  on the consent  calendar."  The  City  is in need of Mr.
Downs'  specialized  skills,  which  are critically  needed  to prepare  the budget  in time  for the next fiscal
year  and before  180  days  have  passed  since  his  retirement  from  the  City  of  South  Pasadena  on
December  31, 2024.  His 30-year  depth  of knowledge  and his personal  contacts  with  all public  agency
and private  entity  stakeholders  are vital  and essential  to the continued  financial  success.  Additionally,
Mr.  Downs  has not  accepted  a retirement  incentive  upon  his  retirement,  which  would  make  him
ineligible  for this consideration  as outlined  in California  Government  Code §7522.56(g).

Mr. Downs'  continued  employment  will  be on a temporary,  part-time  basis and will  remain  at or below
the  960  permitted  hours  per  fiscal  year  a retired  annuitant  may  work  pursuant  to the  California
Governrnent  Code Ep7522.56(d).  His specialized  skills  are needed to ensure there is no backlog  of work
as the budgetary  process  is completed  and that any current  special  projects  to which  he can be assigned
remain  on schedule  and without  internuption.  Additionally,  Mr.  Downs  will  assist  Mr.  Frausto  in his
transition  to the City's  full-time  Director  of Administrative  Services.

  2

  544
 Also,  pursuant  to California  Governrnent  Code  Fp7522.56(d),  Mr.  Downs  pay may not exceed the
maximum  monthly  base salary paid to other employees  performing  comparable  duties  as listed  on  a
publicly  available  pay schedule  equal to the hourly  rate. The maximum  base salary for the Director  of
Administrative  Services  is $18,765  and tlie hourly  equivalent  is $108.26.  Therefore,  Mr. Downs  will
be paid at the rate of $108.26/hour  for duties perforined  as a retired  annuitant  in the capacity  of the
Interim Director of Administrative  Services.

Accordingly,  staff recommends  the City  Council  adopt a Resolution  making  certain  findings  for an
exception  to the 180-day  wait period pursuant to California  Government  Code §§ 7522.56  & 21221.

  quarters of FY 2024-25  to the same period  in FY 2023-24.  The Mid-Year  Financial  Review  also

activity,  as measured  by employment  gains, increases in property  values, and retail sales indicated
growth.  As mentioned  in the FY 2024-25  budget message, revenues were expected  to be on target
based on improved  economic  conditions  and strong recovery  in some areas, such as property  tax.
The City of South Gate anticipated  a moderate  increase  in property  tax and a reduction  in sales
tax. It was therefore  critical  that the City  monitor  its monthly  sales tax receipts  during  the fiscal
year.

 FY 2024-25  Third  Quarter  Revenue  Performance

Overall,  revenues forthe  City are down 7.48% ($2,937,440)  forthe  first tmee quarters of FY 2024-
25 compared  to FY 2023-24.  Outlined  below  is a summary  of the revenue  performance  for the
City's major revenues:

Property  Tax
Through  the end of March  in FY 2024-25,  the City's  second largest revenue,  Property  Tax, was up
6.54% ($574,395)  from FY 2023-24.  The City has received  52.8% of the revenue  and expects the
largest  amount  to come in April  2025.  For FY  2024-25,  the City  budgeted  $17,717,936.  The
estimated  revenue will  increase by $421,135,  to $18.1 million.

hi respect to Secured Property  Taxes, the City received  its Property  Tax installment  in December
2024, representing  40% of what the State expects to receive  for the whole  year. Therefore,  on an
annualized  basis, the City's  estimated  Secured Property  Taxes are slightly  above projections.

Sales Taxes
Taxes (including  Sales Tax Measure  P) are down 4.96% ($820,673)  fl'trough the first three quarters
of FY 2024-25  from last year. Sales Taxes makes up 43.66%  of total General  Fund revenues  and
is the City's  largest revenue  stream. The City budgeted  $29.1 million  for FY 2024-25;  however,
sales tax is projected  to soften. The estimated  revenue  will  be decreased by $1,150,260  to $27.9
million.

  4

  552
 Other  Taxes
Other Tax include  Transient  Occupancy  Tax, Business  License  Tax, Francise  Tax, Commercial
Refuse Franchise  Tax, Real Estate Transfer  Tax, and Materials  Recovetay Facility  Tax. Other Tax
revenues are down 16.56%  ($384,047)  in FY 2024-25  from the same point last year. The estimated
revenue for FY 2024-25  is projected  to increase by $141,360,  to $5.9 million.

Licenses  & Permits
The revenue  from  Licenses  and Permits  saw an 18.05%  decrease ($230,019)  compared  to the
previous  year. The primary  drivers  are a decrease in revenues  from various  building  permits  and
animal  licensing  revenue.  The estimated  revenue  for FY 2024-25  will  decrease by $124,267,  to
$1.6 million.

Fines & Forfeitures
Fines and Forfeihires  decreased by 12.37%  ($118,142)  from last year. The reason for this decrease
is due simply  to a reduction  in Vehicle  Code Fines and Parking  Citations.  The estimated  revenue
for FY 2024-25  will  increase by $131,571,  to $1.5 million.

Use of Money  & Property
Revenue from Use of Money and Property decreased by 63.73% ($2,578,585)  from the same
period last year. The primary reason for this decrease is a smaller return in Interest Earnings and
Bond Interest Earnings.  The estimated  revenue  for FY 2024-25  will  decrease by $140,560,  to $2.4
million.

Intergovernmental
Intergovernmental  revenue increased by 67.86%  ($99,296)  compared  to the previous  year.
Increases were due to better than expected Motor Vehicle In-Lieu Excess revenue and a California
for All Youth  Workforce  Program  Grant. Other Grants had a modest  increase,  that was offset by
a reduction  in POST Reimbursement  revenue.  The estimated  revenue for FY 2024-25  will  increase
by $610,697,  to $765,297.

Fees & Charges
Revenue from Fees and Charges saw a slight increase of 3.16% ($74,625)  in revenue  compared  to
last year. The estimated revenue for FY 2024-25 are projected to decrease by $126,083, to $3.2
million. This category includes fees for various inspections and services, such as inspections, plan
checks, passport  services,  recreation  and sports programs.

Other  Revenues
Other Revenues  category  saw an increase  of 15.83%  ($445,71 1) compared  to the previous  year.
This  group  encompasses  Administrative  Allocations,  Miscellaneous  Reimbursements,  and
Miscellaneous  Revenue.  The largest contributor  to tis  increase was  a project  settlement  recovery
of  $499,931  and  an  expected  contribution  of  $676,524  to  the  Garfield  Avenue  Median
Improvements  project  from  the City  of Downey.  A decrease in Miscellaneous  Reimbursements
partially  offset these increases. The estirnatedrevenue  forFY  2024-25  will  increase by $1,256,943,
to $6.1 million.

Street  Lighting  and Landscaping  Fund
The  Street  Lighting  and  Landscaping  District  assessment  provides  annual  funds  for  the
maintenance  and operation  of traffic  signals, streetlights,  median  landscaping,  street tree trimming,
and tree removals  and replacements.  Each year, the City Council  establishes  LLMD  assessments
which  provide  approximately  $1,998,900  in revenue.  The revenue is collected  through  the County
Assessor's  Office  as part of the property  tax rolls.  However,  for numerous  annual budget  cycles,
the fund costs have exceeded  the revenue,  by upwards  of $1,600,000,  based on the prior  year.
Therefore,  each year, General  Fund monies  have been transferred  into the Street Lighting  and
Landscaping  fund to subsidize  the district.

As a result  of Proposition  218 (Prop  218),  the City  cannot  increase  the proposed  assessments
without  going through  a public  ballot  process. The City has historically  relied on an exemption  of
Prop 218 (passed in 1997),  that allows  the renewal  of the LLMD  assessments,  provided  the rates
are not changed.  If the assessment  rates are changed,  then the balloting  requirements  under  Prop
218 must be fulfilled.  Assessments  have not changed since 1993 and are currently  set at $2.38 per
adjusted front footage.

the City's  personnel  officer,  makes periodic  reviews  of the positions  that are necessary  for the
efficient operation  of the City,  and makes necessaiy  recommendations  for personnel  adjustments
in a Classification  Plan.

License  Clerk  positions,  with  two  incumbents  currently  filling  those  positions,  that require
reclassification  to  Administrative  Services  Clerk  positions  for  the  efficient  operation  of  the
department.  The reclassification  of these positions  has been accepted by the bargaining  group and
the incumbents.  There is no fiscal  impact,  as the salary ranges for the existing  positions  and the
new positions are identical.
